full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiffs respondents, in short, is that the suit property originally belonged to Dhirendra Mohan Chowdhury, Niranjan Kumar Chowdhury and Monindra Kumar Thakur who acquired the property by inheritance and accordingly, record of right was prepared in their names. Dhirendra Mohan Chowdhury and Monindra Kumar Thakur died in the then East Pakistan and Niranjan Kumar Chowdhury left this country for India and their properties were made Khas under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 6. The defendant No. 2 and the leave petitioner as defendant No. 5 appeared in the said suit and filed two separate statements, denying all the material allegations of the plaint. They contended that the plaintiffs' suit is not maintainable and they are not entitled to any relief as prayed for and also contended that the plaintiffs violated the terms of lease agreement. 

 8. Mr. Fazlul Karim, the learned Counsel appearing for the leave petitioner, contended that the plaintiffs' suit challenging the validity of the orders passed by the Board of Land Administration is barred under section 76(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and thereby the learned single Judge acted illegally in failing to notice that the lower appellate Court was wrong in allowing the appeal. It is further contended that the single Judge has fallen in an error of law in holding that section 85 of the said Act is a bar in evicting the plaintiffs from the suit land without considering the provisions of section 92 of the said Act which is applicable to facts of the case empowering the government to evict a tenant from the land. 

 11. It appears that the trial Court dismissed the suit on the ground that the plaintiffs took settlement as nal land for 15 years but, as a matter of fact, the land is not a nal land and, as such, the settlement taken on false statement is not a legal settlement. The trial Court has however found possession of the suit land with the plaintiffs on consideration of evidence on record. The appellate Court being the final court of fact having considered the materials on record rightly found that the plaintiffs took settlement legally and have been possessing the suit property and they have not violated the terms of the settlement. Upon the aforesaid finding the appellate Court decreed the suit holding that the orders dated 29-11-86 and 29-3-88 passed by the defendant No. 1 are illegal and without jurisdiction. 

 14. It appears that the plaintiffs filed the instant suit challenging the two orders passed by the Chairman, Board of Land Administration, Dhaka and that suit cannot be said to be a suit relating to their granting or cancelling of plaintiffs' settlement of land by the government. The plaintiffs got the settlement of land from the government upon proper investigation and enquiry and they have been possessing the same by mutating their names in the record of right. The government has neither cancelled the settlement nor the mutation granted in their favour. The High Court Division also considered the provision of section 85 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. From aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case we are of the view that contention of the petitioner that the plaintiffs' suit is barred under section 76(2) of the said Act is without any substance. 

 15. The submissions made by the learned Counsel for the petitioner with regard to applicability of the provisions of section 85 and section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act cannot also be accepted and hold that the aforesaid provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act cannot be applied in the instant case under the facts and circumstances of the case. We further hold that the plaintiffs-respondents cannot be evicted without due process of law. The High Court Division has also rightly observed that some evil eyes of different persons fell on the suit property to grab the same.
